newsitem.title: USA: NBA-BULLS SWEEP BULLETS, PORTLAND STAYS ALIVE.
newsitem.headline: NBA-BULLS SWEEP BULLETS, PORTLAND STAYS ALIVE.

text.p: Michael Jordan scored 28 points and led a rally capped by Scottie Pippen's driving dunk with 7.4 seconds left that lifted the Chicago Bulls to a 96-95 victory over the Washington Bullets and a sweep of their Eastern Conference first-round series on Wednesday.

Jordan scored 10 points in the final four minutes and was nearly as dominant as he was in Game Two, when he scored 55 points, 20 in the fourth quarter. Pippen, almost a bystander in Game Two, scored 20 points, including the basket that clinched the best-of-five series.
The Bulls advance to the conference semifinals and await the winner of the Atlanta-Detroit series.

"I thought we didn't play to our potential, Jordan said. "What won this was our experience in the playoffs and we were able to utilize our maturity. Their lack of playoff experience is what won this series for us."
Rod Strickland had 24 points and nine assists for Washington, which was hosting its first playoff game in nine years.
The Bullets blew a nine-point lead with four minutes left and were swept by a combined 18 points by the defending NBA champions.
It was the end of an era for the Bullets, who next season are changing their nickname to Wizards.

In Portland, Kenny Anderson scored 17 of his 30 points in the first quarter and the Portland Trail Blazers built a 31-point lead before hanging on to defeat the Los Angeles Lakers, 98-90 and stave off elimination in their Western Conference first-round series.
Los Angeles leads the best-of-five series 2-1.

Anderson, who made his first seven shots, finished 9-of-11 from the floor. He added five assists and five rebounds for Portland, which won a first-round Game Three at home for the third time in the last four years.

Rasheed Wallace added 20 points and Cliff Robinson had 18 for the Trail Blazers, who built a 69-38 lead with eight minutes left in the third quarter. They still maintained a 26-point advantage heading into the final 12 minutes, but saw a furious Lakers rally cut the lead to six in the final minute.

The Trail Blazers won despite getting no points and just five rebounds from starting centre Arvydas Sabonis. Shaquille O'Neal led Los Angeles with 29 points while rookie Kobe Bryant added 22, including 14 in the final period.
Bryant's performance partially offset another bad game by Nick Van Exel, who missed all six of his shots from the field, including three from beyond the arc.

In addition to Van Exel, starting forwards Robert Horry and Elden Campbell also failed to show up. Horry was scoreless in 23 minutes while Campbell had just four points and three rebounds in his 23 minutes.
Game Four is Friday in Portland.
